The three settings, their values (roast light/medium/dark, conche 3/6/11 hours, cacao 55/70/90) and all wording are new and need your chocolatier's OK. Hotspot positions are placeholders. Three new characters need portraits.
title: Tasting Night
opening: Three regulars, three opinions. Dadu's tasting cards are on the table.

intro.p: Once a month Dadu kept the shop open late for a few regulars. They tasted, argued and went home happy. Rafiq Bhai wants the tradition back.

talk: Laila beta! Remember tasting night? Three regulars are coming on Thursday. They each have an opinion, and they never agree.
I remember the noise. I do not remember what any of them asked for.
Easy. Each one asks for a taste, and you make the bar that tastes that way.
A taste is not a recipe. I need to know what makes a bar fruity, or bitter, or mild.
Dadu kept tasting cards, no? One card for each thing he could change.
Then I will read the cards. One at a time.

lines.text: A bar tastes the way you set it. Roast, conche and cacao each change the taste. [[torn:…the cards say how…]]
Nazma Apa: fruity, but not sour. [[torn:…not the all-night kind…]]
Jamal Chacha: bitter, but smooth. [[blur:How bitter?]]
Shumi: mild and sweet, with a toasted taste.
Pour the samples into the moulds. Tap the tray to knock the air out.

workshop.sceneAlt: Dadu's workshop set for a tasting night, with cards and little cups on the table. Tap the glowing objects to remember.
workshop.hintLine: Tap the glowing spots. Dadu left clues all over the workshop.

clues.title: Dadu's roast card
clues.text: Three roasts, three tastes. Light: fruity and bright, with a little sour. Medium: like toasted bread. Dark: smoky and bitter.

clues.title: Dadu's conche card
clues.text: Three lengths, three tastes. 3 hours: sharp and sour. 6 hours: the sour fades, still lively. 11 hours: smooth and mellow.

clues.title: Dadu's cacao card
clues.text: Three strengths, three tastes. 55 percent: mild and sweet. 70 percent: balanced. 90 percent: bitter and strong.

clues.title: The tasting spoons
clues.text: Small wooden spoons, one for each regular. Dadu never let anyone taste with a metal one.

clues.title: The regulars' book
clues.text: Names and favourites in Dadu's pencil. Nazma Apa, always a sour face. Jamal Chacha, never any sugar. Shumi, only the sweet ones.

clues.title: An old photo
clues.text: A faded brown photo of a tasting night. Dadu stands at the back, holding a spoon up to the light.

steps.title: Line 1: Nazma Apa
steps.prompt: Nazma Apa has asked for a taste. Pick a setting in each row, then make the sample.
steps.say: Nazma Apa, retired schoolteacher: "Fruity, please, but not sour. And not the all-night kind. I like a lively chocolate."

options.name: Light roast
options.taste: fruity and bright, with a little sour

free.cacao: Nazma Apa has no opinion about cacao, so any choice works.

params.unfilled: Pick a setting in every row first.

feedback.correct: Nazma Apa tastes it and her face stays calm. "Fruity, and not one bit sour. Lively, like I asked."

hints: Each of Dadu's cards in the Workshop covers one setting. Nazma Apa's two words match two different cards.
Light roast tastes fruity. A 6 hour conche fades the sour and stays lively. Cacao can be anything.

steps.title: Line 2: Jamal Chacha
steps.prompt: Jamal Chacha wants something different. Pick a setting in each row, then make the sample.
steps.say: Jamal Chacha, who runs the rickshaw garage: "Bitter, please, but smooth. I have no patience for rough."

options.name: Light roast
options.taste: fruity and bright, with a little sour

free.roast: Jamal Chacha has no opinion about roast, so any choice works.

params.unfilled: Pick a setting in every row first.

feedback.correct: Jamal Chacha closes his eyes. "Bitter, and not one rough edge. This one I will carry home."

hints: Two cards again, but different ones from the last customer. Look for the words bitter and smooth.
90 percent cacao is bitter and strong. An 11 hour conche is smooth and mellow. Roast can be anything.

steps.title: Line 3: Shumi
steps.prompt: Shumi is the last regular. Pick a setting in each row, then make the sample.
steps.say: Shumi, a university student: "Mild and sweet, please. But I want it to taste toasted, like fresh bread."

options.name: Light roast
options.taste: fruity and bright, with a little sour

free.conche: Shumi has no opinion about conching, so any choice works.

params.unfilled: Pick a setting in every row first.

feedback.correct: Shumi takes a second bite before she says anything. "Sweet, and still toasty. Can I take the rest to the library?"

hints: Roast and cacao this time. Which card talks about toasted bread, and which about mild and sweet?
Medium roast tastes like toasted bread. 55 percent cacao is mild and sweet. Conche can be anything.

steps.title: Last line: mould
steps.prompt: Three samples are ready. Tap the tray six times to knock the air out.
steps.say: Pour the samples, then knock the air out.

feedback.correct: Three small bars, three different tastes, all from the same three settings.

talk: "Fruity and lively. Dadu would have given you a nod."
"Bitter and smooth. Do you make this every week?"
Only a month ago I did not know what a roast did. Tonight I tasted it before I made it.
recipe: Fruity, not sour: light roast, 6 hour conche
Bitter, but smooth: 90 percent cacao, 11 hour conche
Mild and sweet, toasted: 55 percent cacao, medium roast
Roast, conche and cacao each change the taste
reveal.realFact: In real life, roast, conching time and cacao work together to shape flavour, and makers tune them as a set. The words fruity, nutty and bitter are how tasters describe the result.
